title: Tenant scope must survive jobs caches and storage

criteria: Derive active membership server-side and authorize every document against the tenant.
Carry tenant scope into worker queries and recheck revocation before sensitive execution or delivery.
Scope object keys and cache ownership; use authorized signed downloads.
Reject the claim that ORM types establish authorization and specify two-tenant negative tests.

rubric.pass_if: Explicitly rejects client organizationId as authority and authorizes all selected rows.
Covers job revocation plus tenant-specific object and cache access.
Includes negative tests for tenant-swapped IDs and sends unresolved risks to security review.

anti_patterns: Accept login or Prisma types as sufficient isolation.
Share a public latest.zip across tenants.
source: Original case derived from Supabase RLS and the inspected Trigger.dev ownership model; https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security
